newsitem.title: UK: British Biotech says Noble departs amicably.
newsitem.headline: British Biotech says Noble departs amicably.

text.p: British Biotech Plc said on Thursday that the departure of its finance director James Noble was "amicable," and something that he had considered carefully.

In a telephone interview with Reuters following news of Noble's resignation which surprised analysts and depressd the company's share price, chief executive officer Keith McCullagh said Noble had "been considering his departure for some time, but his decision has only happened this week."
Noble also denied a newspaper report that the company would be returning to the market to seek further funding.
McCullagh said Noble has "some opportunites which he would like to explore."
"His interests and skills are in corporate finance an investor relations and the management of that phase of growth. That is what he likes to do," McCullagh said.
He added that British Bitoech had started the search for a replacement through head hunters.
"We are looking for somebody who has got strong international operating experience for a major company which has a range of subsidiaries and which is building revenues and profits," McCullagh said.

He added that as British Biotech built up its marketing in anticipation of the launch of its two lead products, acute pancreatitis drug Lexipafant and cancer treatment Marimastat, the role would be "a more traditional finance director than we have had in the past."
McCullagh also said there was no need to seek further funding, noting that the group had "just under 200 million stg in cash reserves and that is a substantial amount of money."
He repeated the view that last year's 143 million stg rights issue would provide sufficient funds to commercialise the group's lead products.
